stories.title: Human Understanding
stories.excerpt: Two chess players laughed at the moon pulling the tides, then happily believed in a sponge mountain.

stories.title: Two Approaches
stories.excerpt: An agnostic wanted the orange; Swamiji wanted the mango. Both were after the juice of life.

stories.title: Not a drop of Water
stories.excerpt: A holy man handed Swamiji a rain forecast and told him to squeeze it. Nothing came out.

stories.title: Where were these rishis?
stories.excerpt: A London friend asked why India's sages never came to teach England. Swamiji's reply was sharp.

stories.title: Story of the Deluge
stories.excerpt: A tiny fish begged the sage Manu for shelter, and kept growing until it filled the ocean.

stories.title: Until You Know God
stories.excerpt: Socrates said the greatest study is man. A visiting Brahmin asked him one sharp question back.

stories.title: Freedom—the Only Condition of Growth
stories.excerpt: Buddha denounced the gods for eighty years and died peacefully. What does that say about India?

stories.title: ‘I Want Religion’
stories.excerpt: A young man kept saying he wanted religion. His teacher showed him what wanting really feels like.

stories.title: The Salt Doll
stories.excerpt: A doll made of salt set out to measure the ocean's depth. It never came back.

stories.title: The Bugle Sound
stories.excerpt: A proud stag boasted of his mighty horns, until he heard the hunter's bugle.

stories.title: ‘Thou art That’
stories.excerpt: A queen sang one line to her babies every night. It shaped all four of their lives.

stories.title: Bondage of Nature
stories.excerpt: A Frenchman proudly served his guest a glowing glass of fine old wine. It was castor oil.

stories.title: The Old Chinaman
stories.excerpt: After sixty years in a dungeon, an old prisoner was set free, and begged to go back.

stories.title: The Story of Vilvamangala
stories.excerpt: He crossed a raging river on a corpse and climbed a cobra for love, then found a greater love.

stories.title: Lingering Hope
stories.excerpt: A king was asked: what is the most wonderful thing in the world? The answer was one word.

stories.title: Lion and Sheep
stories.excerpt: A lion cub raised by sheep grew up bleating and eating grass, until it saw its reflection.

stories.title: Fisherwomen in a Florist’s House
stories.excerpt: Stranded in a house full of flowers, some fisherwomen couldn't sleep until they smelled their fish baskets.

stories.title: Non-attachment
stories.excerpt: A polite mosquito apologised to a bull for sitting on its horn. The bull just laughed.

stories.title: True Contentment
stories.excerpt: On a stormy night, a comfortable cowherd sang to the rain. The Buddha, outside, sang back.

stories.title: From Gross to Subtle
stories.excerpt: Locked in a tower to die, a minister escaped using a beetle, some honey and a thread.

stories.title: Neither Good Nor Evil
stories.excerpt: Looking at the moon, a clergyman saw church spires. A young lady saw something else entirely.

stories.title: Story of a Young sannyasin
stories.excerpt: A yogi could burn birds with a glance. A housewife and a butcher taught him what real power is.

stories.title: ‘Getting Nearer to the Lord’
stories.excerpt: Why bless the people who insult you? Swamiji's surprising answer involves a mother monkey.

stories.title: The Story of Jada Bharata
stories.excerpt: A king who gave up a whole empire got hooked on a pet deer, and it cost him lifetimes.

stories.title: Why We Disagree
stories.excerpt: A frog who had never left his well was sure nothing could be bigger than it.

stories.title: Love for God
stories.excerpt: His wife asked what God had ever given him. His answer: Do I love a mountain for profit?

stories.title: ‘It is also Yours’
stories.excerpt: A thief stole a saint's cooking pot. The saint chased him down to give him the other one.

stories.title: Four Travellers
stories.excerpt: Three travellers leapt over a high wall laughing. Only the fourth came back to tell.

stories.title: ‘I cannot Trade in Love’
stories.excerpt: Exiled to the forest, Yudhishthira was asked why the good suffer. His answer was a mountain range.

stories.title: Be Pure and Love Everyone
stories.excerpt: Five young men argued over the one true path to God. Buddha asked: has anyone seen Him?

stories.title: The Highest Love
stories.excerpt: A lover knocked and was turned away three times. The fourth time, his answer opened the door.

stories.title: Nishtha or Devotion to One Ideal
stories.excerpt: Hanuman knew Krishna and Rama were the same God. He still wanted only Rama.

stories.title: The Way of One-pointed Devotion
stories.excerpt: Some people chase one exciting idea after another. The pearl-oyster catches a single raindrop and goes deep.

stories.title: Courage To Be
stories.excerpt: An emperor threatened to kill an old sage. The sage just smiled.

stories.title: Truth Will Be Out, Sooner Or Later
stories.excerpt: Every courtier poured water instead of milk, sure that nobody would notice. By morning, everyone did.

stories.title: Guru Nanak’s Insight
stories.excerpt: The mullah's lips said 'Allah, Allah'. Guru Nanak smiled, because he knew where the mullah's mind was.

stories.title: Great Indian Women
stories.excerpt: A Brahmin girl who led armies, and a queen in full armour who drove back an empire.

stories.title: Arise, Awake!
stories.excerpt: Six months in a new land turned a frightened immigrant into a man who walked tall. Why?

stories.title: Thief and a Non-killer
stories.excerpt: A master who preached non-violence saved a thief from a beating, then ordered him drowned.

stories.title: Believe in Yourselves
stories.excerpt: A struggling clerk twice tried to end his life. Then he started believing in himself.

stories.title: Concept of Heaven
stories.excerpt: In the Norse heaven, warriors hunt the same boar every single day, forever. Sound like paradise?

stories.title: Solon and Croesus
stories.excerpt: A rich king called himself the happiest man alive. A sage told him to wait.

stories.title: What Joy Really Is
stories.excerpt: A man still worth a million pounds took his life because he felt poor. What is joy, really?

stories.title: And This Is Maya
stories.excerpt: Narada went to fetch water and lived twelve years in half an hour.

stories.title: Our Predicament
stories.excerpt: The Lord became a pig, loved the mud, and refused to come home.

stories.title: Resolving Our Conflicts
stories.excerpt: A fox spoiled a poor man's feast. The mullah's cure: let a dog spoil it too.

stories.title: Going Round and Round
stories.excerpt: A blindfolded bullock walks in circles all day, chasing straw it can never reach.

stories.title: The Mirage of the World
stories.excerpt: For a month Swamiji admired lakes in the desert. Then he tried to drink from one.

stories.title: Alice in Wonderland
stories.excerpt: Swamiji loved Alice in Wonderland, and saw the whole world in its delightful nonsense.

stories.title: Two Birds
stories.excerpt: Two golden birds on one tree: one calm at the top, one restlessly pecking fruit below.

stories.title: ‘I am Discovered’
stories.excerpt: A shoemaker was told to keep quiet so no one would guess his caste. It didn't go well.

stories.title: Intensity of Prayer
stories.excerpt: A man at prayer is stepped on by a girl in a hurry. Her reply silences him.

stories.title: All Power is within
stories.excerpt: A girl floats in mid-air, and a suspicious Governor swings his sword beneath her.

stories.title: The Tartar Inside
stories.excerpt: A soldier proudly captures an enemy, then can't bring him in, or get away himself.

stories.title: The Noseless Saint
stories.excerpt: Why wouldn't Pavhari Baba leave his cave to help the world? He answered with a wicked joke.

stories.title: All Powers are in the Mind
stories.excerpt: A man reads sealed questions, and another pulls baskets of grapes from under a blanket.

stories.title: Be Like a Pearl Oyster
stories.excerpt: Oysters rise to catch one special raindrop, then sink deep to turn it into a pearl.

stories.title: Pratika Or Symbolism
stories.excerpt: A learned yogi mocks a cowherd with a joke answer about God. The cowherd takes it seriously.

stories.title: A Case of Complete Self-sacrifice
stories.excerpt: A half-golden mongoose calls the grandest sacrifice ever held a fake. Here's why.

stories.title: The Bell-Eared Demon (Ghanta Karna)
stories.excerpt: A devotee hated another god's name so much he tied bells to his ears to drown it out.

stories.title: Each is Great in His Own Place
stories.excerpt: Who is greater, the monk or the householder? A king travels far to find out.

stories.title: Shraddha or Genuine Faith
stories.excerpt: In a Kashmir village, Swamiji asks two people their religion. Their answers reveal something deep.

stories.title: Sita-Rama, the Ideal Couple
stories.excerpt: A forest sage praises Sita for obeying her husband. Sita gently gives a deeper answer.

stories.title: A Heroic Act
stories.excerpt: Two tales from Rajput history: a daring elopement, and a queen who chose fire over capture.

stories.title: Raksha Bandhan
stories.excerpt: Threatened by an emperor's army, a Rajput girl fights back with silken threads.

stories.title: The Status of Women in the Vedas
stories.excerpt: At King Janaka's court, the sharpest questioner of the great sage was a young woman.

stories.title: Be Active First
stories.excerpt: A dull man asks Swamiji how to find God. The surprising advice: first learn to lie!

stories.title: We, Not the World, Get Straightened Out
stories.excerpt: A man gets a ghost that grants every wish, but it eats him if it runs out of work.

stories.title: Narada and Two Aspirants
stories.excerpt: One seeker weeps at four more births. Another dances at countless more. Guess who gets freedom.

stories.title: Universal Brotherhood
stories.excerpt: Two brothers drinking in secret keep shouting 'Quiet!' at each other. Guess who wakes up.

stories.title: Sin of Killing Cow
stories.excerpt: A man kills a cow in anger, then tries to pin the blame on a god.

stories.title: So He Has Also Followed Suit
stories.excerpt: A young critic suddenly praises the Gita. Sri Ramakrishna knows exactly why.

stories.title: Who Serves the Lord the Best
stories.excerpt: One gardener flatters the master; the other quietly grows his fruit. Which one does the master love?

stories.title: It is the Heart that Moves, Truly
stories.excerpt: Stranded Burmese travellers in London are rescued by one woman, and then a whole nation.

stories.title: Strength is the Test
stories.excerpt: An astrologer tells a king he has six months to live. One quick-witted minister calls his bluff.

stories.title: Do Something Religious
stories.excerpt: A ship is sinking and the crew begs the church elder to do something religious. He passes the hat.

stories.title: We are Lions, not Sheep
stories.excerpt: Raised among sheep, a young lion bleats and eats grass, until another lion shows him his reflection.

stories.title: Satyakama’s Story
stories.excerpt: A boy with no family name tells the plain truth, and the whole universe becomes his teacher.

stories.title: How Upakosala Got Knowledge
stories.excerpt: Too sad to eat while his teacher is away, a student hears the sacred fire speak to him.

stories.title: ‘You Have Known the Truth’
stories.excerpt: Ignored for three days, then pampered for eight, young Shuka stays exactly the same. Then comes the milk test.

stories.title: Gods and Demons
stories.excerpt: A god and a demon hear the same teaching: you are the Self. Only one keeps asking questions.

stories.title: A Fable About Buddha
stories.excerpt: The gods pile a sacrificial fire on Buddha's chest to destroy him. They discover purity cannot be killed.

stories.title: Yajnavalkya and Maitreyi
stories.excerpt: Offered all of her husband's wealth, Maitreyi asks one question: will this make me immortal?

stories.title: The Story of Vedanta
stories.excerpt: From tribal gods to the God of the universe: Swamiji traces humanity's long search for something higher.

stories.title: The Story of Nachiketa
stories.excerpt: Given to Death by an angry father, a boy turns down kingdoms and riches to ask one question.

stories.title: Nature is Like Ferris Wheel
stories.excerpt: Swamiji looks at Chicago's giant Ferris Wheel and sees the whole journey of the soul.

stories.title: We Are Like Silkworms
stories.excerpt: We spin our own cocoons and get trapped inside. But the story doesn't end there.

stories.title: The Intense Desire To Be Free
stories.excerpt: A teacher holds his student underwater to show him what real longing for God feels like.

stories.title: ‘Where Shall It Fall?’
stories.excerpt: An examiner asks why the earth doesn't fall. One little girl's reply stumps him completely.

stories.title: Eat the Mangoes
stories.excerpt: Some visitors to a mango orchard count leaves and twigs. One sensible man just eats the fruit.

stories.title: The Passing Away of Buddha
stories.excerpt: Offered a meal by a despised outcaste, the dying Buddha eats it gladly, and calls him a benefactor.

stories.title: Have You Seen God?
stories.excerpt: A son returns home listing all the sciences he has mastered. His father sends him straight back.

stories.title: ‘Whosoever Will Save His Life’
stories.excerpt: A rich young man asks Jesus the way to eternal life, and walks away sad at the answer.

stories.title: Buddha’s Counsel
stories.excerpt: Five scholars argue over whose scripture shows the way to God. Buddha settles it with one question.

stories.title: The Transformation
stories.excerpt: A highway robber asks his family to share the weight of his sins. Their answer changes everything.

stories.title: The Story of Ramayana
stories.excerpt: A grieving dove, a sage's cry of pity, and the first poem ever sung: India's oldest epic.

stories.title: The Danger of Frauds
stories.excerpt: A rich man claimed God told him to take a painting. The owner had a divine message too.

stories.title: A Leader Leads by Example
stories.excerpt: Well-armed, trained soldiers lost the battle. A British general explained exactly why.

stories.title: Blind Men and Elephant
stories.excerpt: Five blind men touched one elephant and came away with five different animals, and a fight.

stories.title: ‘This is Fanaticism’
stories.excerpt: A young woman in Chicago was sure she'd found the cure for every evil in the world.

stories.title: The Greatest Birth
stories.excerpt: Why would even the gods have to be born as humans? Swamiji explains the value of being human.

stories.title: Your Doctrine Of Heredity!
stories.excerpt: A boy who escaped horror in Africa gave a brilliant speech in America. So much for 'heredity'.

stories.title: The Story of Mahabharata
stories.excerpt: Cousins at war, a rigged dice game, a love stronger than death, and a king who wouldn't abandon his dog.

stories.title: Real Prayer is Unconditional
stories.excerpt: A king wanted to give a sage a gift. Then the sage heard the king pray.

stories.title: Judge Ye Not
stories.excerpt: The English hated French bull-fights; the French threw out English boxers. Swamiji saw a lesson.

stories.title: A Calcutta Youth in Father-in-law’s House
stories.excerpt: A city boy drank a glass of milk before dinner. Then the drums started and the truth came out.
